newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher on back of Dow.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher on back of Dow.

text.p: Argentine stocks, which were locked in a tight range Monday, climbed at the close on a powerful late surge which propelled the Dow to a record high, dealers said.

"The U.S. markets fuelled the bolsa at the close, although the rise here was tempered by the selective mood prevailing ahead of the arrival of more company results," said Emilio Alessandro at brokers Alessandro.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 0.8 percent to 738.28, against a 2.0 percent leap in the Dow which closed at a record 7214.49 points.

"We might follow through more on the Dow's gains tomorrow, because ADRs today tended to lag the rest of the U.S. market," another trader said. "However, we don't expect a rally, considering that local investors are cautious after last week's 2.3 percent blue-chip rise."
The broad market index advanced 0.7 percent in the session, with winners outpacing losers 23 to 15 and 19 issues closing flat.
Floor volume picked up to 20.7 million pesos from 18.5 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover dwindled to 70.2 million pesos from 115.5 million Friday.

Top main-tier performers were steelmakers Siderca and Siderar, which rose 4.7 percent and 1.0 percent, respectively, carmakers Ciadea and Sevel, up 3.6 percent and 2.3 percent each, and holding company Perez Companc and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, both up 1.2 percent.
MerVal losers were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, construction stock Polledo and Bansud Bank, off 4.9 percent, 0.9 percent and 0.7 percent, respectively.
